problem: J_A = −D_AB dc_A/dz is presented as the general first law for molar diffusion flux relative to the molar average velocity. That form is valid only when the total molar concentration c is constant. In general the molar form is J_A = −c D_AB dy_A/dz. The text also says to use the molar-fraction form when c is nearly constant, which reverses the real limitation.
fix: State the general molar form as J_A = −c D_AB dy_A/dz (or ∂y_A/∂z). State that J_A = −D_AB dc_A/dz is the special case when c is constant. Update Quiz Q1 to use the general form or explicitly assume constant c.

where: Section 1, sentence introducing cA = c yA
problem: cA = c yA is the definition of mole fraction for any mixture, not only an ideal mixture. The wording can make students think nonideal mixtures do not obey it.
fix: Say: By definition, cA = c yA; when c is constant, dcA/dz = c dyA/dz.
